title: Independent qualification of Marketing SDK parity foundation
delivery: workspace-only; candidate qualification, not live or published cutover

source_coverage.fresh_inspection: Only this SDK checkout: core/server/React, SQL adapters/schema/migrations, provider and service execution, budget/event/reporting code, existing runners and consumer fixture.
source_coverage.supplied_context: Pinned-source comparison completed in KB marketing-sdk-migration-parity-baseline-20261006, review-state revision 1, entry f539c339-4ca9-42ac-8f40-ad6fce8b53e5. ERP and Agent conclusions are supplied source-backed context, not fresh source inspection by this reviewer.
source_coverage.scope_confirmed: Handrail current-context read confirmed this SDK project/work request and authentication snapshot 08346f8bc724. No repository AGENTS.md was found.

findings.before: Store.postgres always executes schema DDL, preventing startup with a restricted runtime role.
findings.after: Added Store.openExistingPostgres and separate Store.migratePostgres. Open-existing performs read-only schema/version validation and session SET statements; rejects missing/outdated/future/incomplete schema. Legacy Store.postgres remains migrating for compatibility. Reference opener supports explicit open-existing mode.

findings.before: Source receipt identity included outcome kind, so a different kind and new request ID could mint another event. Imported IDs without request receipts could be overwritten by another source event.
findings.after: New source evidence keys bind source plus receipt, independent of kind. Immutable input digest includes kind, person, purpose, QA and attribution input. Legacy evidence keys remain readable; imported IDs and unknown attribution are preserved; conflicting source receipts fail closed.

findings.before: UI always requested campaign start/end for provider sync, including unsupported future or partial-day windows; results without a snapshot had no explicit window basis.
findings.after: UI defaults to exact completed account-local days contained within campaign boundaries, disables sync for full first-party windows, and labels partial/open result windows. DST and exact-boundary behavior is tested. Added explicit selector accessible name after browser regression.

findings.before: The disposable browser runner was reachable only through MariaDB, which is absent.
findings.after: Existing PostgreSQL runner now accepts --browser and uses the existing browser/app fixture. No new app, framework, resource binding or package check script.

findings.before: Blank/whitespace provider metric strings and booleans could coerce to zero through Number(), silently converting malformed evidence into known spend.
findings.after: Metric aggregation accepts numbers or nonblank numeric strings only; malformed fields remain null while genuine numeric zero remains zero.

adversarial_review.assessment: Daily and lifetime remain separate; explicit budgets require host policy and exact current aggregate evidence. No public configure/observe/coverage command exists. PostgreSQL cross-connection portfolio contention, same-name project scope isolation, unknown/missing/stale and currency/timezone/interval mismatch, outer rollback, policy changes after approval and spend changes before provider writes are exercised. Existing budgets.ts implementation retained.

Lease loss retains unknown holds; actual killed-process activation retains a held reservation across recovery; reconciliation promotes it to active; lost pause acknowledgment retains active capacity until observed pause. Pre-dispatch blocked operations release only their own hold. New activation after pause uses new authority; consumed packets/new request keys cannot replay.

Initial HTTP-fixture readback compares campaign and group account, organization, objective, type/format, bid/cost type, daily and lifetime money/currency, schedule, targeting and creative. Added group account/lifetime drift cases. Lost acknowledgment reconciliation performs reads; versioned v1 snapshot digests continue to support legacy pause without daily fabrication or provider-ID/material rewrites. Missing legacy IDs/digests remain fenced rather than guessed.

Submissions count stable source/event receipts separately from people; acquisition and recruitment coverage/outcomes stay separate; explicit QA flags exclude production metrics; legacy leads retains people semantics. Unknown attribution is retained and absent coverage/empty provider response stays unknown. Current/future provider days reject before native network reads.

Core/headless remains browser-safe; server APIs are additive; normal build emits declarations. Clean consumer projection checks strict types, runtime imports and browser graph isolation. Existing browser fixture exercises widths 1440/390/320, budget review, Create/Launch/Results, outcomes, read recovery and no overflow.

integration.options: export type PostgresStoreOptions = pg.PoolConfig & { schema?: string }
integration.legacy: Store.postgres and reference opener default migrate deliberately retain automatic migration behavior; new ordinary host integrations must choose the explicit open-existing path.
integration.consumer_revision: Uncommitted candidate only. No publishable revision exists from this delivery. Eventual consumer must install public HTTPS Git at the full released commit SHA with matching lockfile and normal prepare build.

migration_and_rollback: No SQL schema files or migration version changed. Trusted migration applies existing schema 1/session migration 2 atomically under the advisory lock; ordinary open-existing performs no DDL. Only disposable test databases were migrated.

Host must provision the same SDK schema using trusted migration credentials, then run with schema USAGE, base-table DML, sequence USAGE/SELECT and view SELECT. Schema owner privileges are not required at runtime. Schema DDL must not change under the running executor.

Use one executor and one transaction-guard domain for portfolio members. Cross-database portfolios, active-commitment import, policy rollover and less conservative spend netting are not implemented. Policies with held/active reservations cannot change. Provider daily pacing is not an exact intraday hard spending guarantee.

Retain original material revisions, provider IDs, imported attribution and exclusion evidence, source event identities, requests, leases, reservations, outbox and session revocations. Do not re-ingest legacy data through fresh attribution or clear unknown effects to unblock execution.

Quiesce dispatch and reconcile unknown effects before rollback/cutover, then prove single-writer routing. v0.1.4 cannot safely dispatch typed-budget campaigns. Read-only rollback is possible only while preserving all records and acknowledging older reporting semantics. Do not drop revocation state or perform destructive down-migrations.
remaining_gates: MariaDB and MariaDB browser verification unavailable while mariadbd is absent; PostgreSQL does not substitute for that dialect.
Public HTTPS full-SHA consumer install qualification after separately authorized release; no commit/push/PR/deploy in this delivery.
Host-specific migration/data mapping, active commitments, historical attribution/exclusion shadow comparisons and rollback before live cutover.
Provider feature expansion including Meta interests/Instagram/objectives and LinkedIn facets/documents/conversions remains deferred.
Recruitment provider publication, full UI/drafts overhaul, lifecycle rollover/external drift recovery, generation controls, Website/A-B and optional qualified Agent/Vault onboarding remain deferred.
No live provider/API actions, datastore access, advertising/budget changes or credential/access expansion performed.
verification_policy: Focused regression and sequential full checks, each below the saved five-minute limit. No configured check or package-script changes. Exact final outcomes, intermediate failures, manifest and changed-file hashes are recorded in artifacts/parity-review-handoff.json to avoid a self-referential source hash.
